definition_en: to pay someone to work for you, or to make use of something
core_image: 工厂门口，经理把工作牌递给新工人
scene: 这家工厂雇用了三百多名工人。The factory employs more than three hundred workers.
sceneCN: 这里 employ 是「雇用」（第 1 个义项：付钱请人工作）；句意：这家工厂雇用了三百多名工人。

collocations.zh: 充分就业的；全神贯注的

senses.title: To hire someone for work
senses.definition: to give someone a job and pay them for their work
senses.definitionCN: 给某人工作并为其劳动付钱
senses.example: The company employs fifty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司雇用了五十个人。
senses.why: Work is exchanged for money, so the word first names the act of taking a person into paid service.
senses.whyCN: 劳动与金钱交换，因此这个词首先指把人纳入有薪工作的行为。

senses.title: To make use of something
senses.definition: to use a method, tool, or material for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的使用方法、工具或材料
senses.example: They employ a simple method.
senses.exampleCN: 他们采用一种简单的方法。
senses.why: A tool is taken into service much as a worker is, so the hiring sense extends to using things.
senses.whyCN: 工具像工人一样被纳入使用，因此雇用义扩展到使用事物。

senses.title: To keep oneself busy
senses.definition: to keep oneself or another person occupied with an activity
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或他人忙于某项活动
senses.example: She employed herself in reading.
senses.exampleCN: 她埋头读书。
senses.why: Time and attention are put to work, so the word can describe being fully occupied.
senses.whyCN: 时间和注意力被投入工作，因此这个词也能描述全神贯注的状态。

intro.en: Employ comes from a Latin word meaning to fold in or involve, which passed through French.
intro.cn: employ 来自拉丁语中意为「卷入、包含」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Implicare means to fold in or involve.
items.cn: implicare 意为卷入、包含。

items.en: Employer develops the sense of using or engaging a person.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 发展出使用、聘用某人的含义。

items.en: English borrows employ with the sense of using or occupying.
items.cn: 英语借入 employ，表示使用或占用。

items.en: The word settles into the modern sense of hiring workers.
items.cn: 在近代早期，这个词固定为雇用工人的现代义。

items.en: Employ now covers hiring, using, and keeping busy.
items.cn: 现代英语中，employ 涵盖雇用、使用和使忙于。

note.en: Employ hires or uses; hire is the plain everyday word, and use focuses on tools.
note.cn: employ 表示雇用或使用；hire 是日常说法，use 侧重使用工具。

senses.exampleCN: 好老师让学生更有能力。
senses.why: Power can be personal as well as official, so the word also covers growing confidence.
senses.whyCN: 权力既可以是官方的，也可以是个人的，因此这个词也涵盖自信的增长。

senses.title: To enable an action
senses.definition: to make an action or process possible for someone
senses.definitionCN: 使某人能够采取行动或推进过程
senses.example: The new tool empowers small teams.
senses.exampleCN: 新工具让小团队也能做成事。
senses.why: Once people have the means, they can act, so empowerment is also practical enablement.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们有了手段就能行动，因此赋权也是实际上的使能。

intro.en: Empower adds the Latin prefix em- to the Germanic word power, meaning to put power into someone.
intro.cn: empower 在日耳曼词 power 前加拉丁前缀 em-，意为把权力放入某人身上。

items.en: Povoir, the ancestor of power, means to be able.
items.cn: power 的祖先 povoir 意为能够。

items.en: Power names ability and authority.
items.cn: power 指能力与权威。

items.en: The verb empower appears with the sense of giving authority.
items.cn: 动词 empower 出现，表示授予权力。

items.en: Empower is used in law and politics for granted rights.
items.cn: 在十九世纪，empower 用于法律与政治中授予权利。

items.en: The word now also means building confidence and ability.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词也指建立自信与能力。

note.en: Empower gives power or confidence; enable removes barriers, and authorize gives formal permission.
note.cn: empower 给予权力或信心，enable 移除障碍，authorize 给予正式许可。

normalIntro.en: Empower means to put power into someone, whether official or personal.
normalIntro.cn: empower 意为把权力放入某人身上，无论官方权力还是个人力量。

normal.cn: 好老师让学生更有能力。

normal.en: The team was empowered to decide.

abstract.en: Picture a key placed in an open hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被放进张开的手掌。

abstract.en: See a student speaking with new confidence.
abstract.cn: 想象学生带着新的自信发言。

abstract.en: Think of power flowing from one person to another.
abstract.cn: 想象力量从一个人流向另一个人。

examples.en: The law empowers citizens with more rights.
examples.cn: 这项法律赋予公民更多权利。

examples.en: Good teachers empower their students.
examples.cn: 好老师让学生更有能力。

examples.en: The new tool empowers small teams.
examples.cn: 新工具让小团队也能做成事。

root: 前缀 em-（使进入）+ power（力量、权力）。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers official authorization, personal confidence, and practical enablement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖官方授权、个人自信，以及实际的使能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key placed in an open hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙被放进张开的手掌。

branches.en: The base sense is granting official power.
branches.cn: 基本义是授予官方权力。

branches.en: Power also grows as personal confidence.
branches.cn: 权力也以个人自信的形式增长。

branches.en: Having means makes action possible.
branches.cn: 拥有手段让行动成为可能。

branches.en: Authority and confidence both free a person to act.
branches.cn: 权威与自信都让人得以行动。

branches.en: Confidence turns ability into practice.
branches.cn: 自信把能力变成实践。

intro.en: Empower joins the prefix em-, meaning into, with the noun power.
intro.cn: empower 把意为「进入」的前缀 em- 与名词 power 结合。

latinIntro.en: The prefix em- is a Latin form of in-, while power itself comes from Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 em- 是拉丁前缀 in- 的变体，而 power 本身来自古法语。

items.example: The prefix em- puts power in.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 em- 把力量放入。

items.example: Power is the heart of empower.
items.exampleCN: power 是 empower 的核心。
empowering 标记正在进行的动作。

definition_en: containing nothing, or to remove everything from something
core_image: 演出散场后，空荡荡的座椅一排排延伸到黑暗里
scene: 演出结束后，礼堂变得空荡荡的。After the show the hall was empty.
sceneCN: 这里 empty 是「空的」（第 1 个义项：里面没有东西或人）；句意：演出结束后，礼堂变得空荡荡的。

senses.title: Containing nothing
senses.definition: having nothing or no one inside
senses.definitionCN: 里面没有任何东西或人
senses.example: The box is empty.
senses.exampleCN: 盒子是空的。
senses.why: The word points to a space with its contents removed, so the container looks bare.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指向内容被移走的空间，因此容器显得光秃秃的。

senses.title: To remove everything
senses.definition: to take out all the contents of something
senses.definitionCN: 把某物里面的东西全部取出
senses.example: Please empty the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 请把垃圾桶倒空。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a verb when someone causes the empty state.
senses.whyCN: 当人造成空的状态时，形容词就变成了动词。

senses.title: Hollow or without meaning
senses.definition: lacking real meaning, feeling, or value
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏真正意义、感情或价值的
senses.example: His words sounded empty.
senses.exampleCN: 他的话听起来很空洞。
senses.why: An empty container has nothing inside, so the image extends to words or feelings with no substance.
senses.whyCN: 空容器里面什么都没有，于是这一意象延伸到没有实质的言语或情感。

intro.en: Empty comes from an Old English word for leisure or vacant time, then shifted to vacant space.
intro.cn: empty 来自古英语中表示闲暇或空闲时间的词，后来转为空无一物。

items.en: Æmettig means free from work or occupation.
items.cn: ǣmettig 意为没有工作、空闲的。

items.en: The sense widens from free time to vacant space.
items.cn: 词义从空闲时间扩展到空的空间。

items.en: Empty becomes the standard adjective for containers with nothing in them.
items.cn: 在近代早期，empty 成为空容器的标准形容词。

items.en: The word gains the figurative sense of hollow or meaningless.
items.cn: 这个词获得空洞、无意义的比喻义。

items.en: Empty works as both adjective and verb.
items.cn: 当代英语中，empty 兼作形容词与动词。

note.en: Empty means nothing inside; vacant means not occupied, and bare means without covering.
note.cn: empty 指里面没东西，vacant 指无人占用，bare 指没有覆盖物。

normalIntro.en: Empty describes a space with nothing in it, and the verb clears the space.
normalIntro.cn: empty 描述里面没有东西的空间，动词义则是清空这个空间。

normal.en: The room was empty after the show.

abstract.en: Picture rows of seats in an empty theatre.
abstract.cn: 想象空剧院里一排排座椅。

abstract.en: See an open box with nothing inside.
abstract.cn: 想象打开后空无一物的盒子。

abstract.en: Think of words that sound loud but mean little.
abstract.cn: 想象响亮却没有内容的言语。

examples.en: The box is empty.
examples.cn: 盒子是空的。

examples.en: Please empty the bin.
examples.cn: 请把垃圾桶倒空。

examples.en: His words sounded empty.
examples.cn: 他的话听起来很空洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安普提」——箱子提起来很轻，因为里面空了；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 ǣmettig（空闲的），中古英语时期转为「空无一物」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers vacant space, the act of clearing it, and the feeling of hollowness.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖空的空间、清空的动作，以及空洞的感觉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of vacant seats after a show.
core.cn: 核心意象：演出后一排排空座椅。

branches.en: The base sense is a space with nothing inside.
branches.cn: 基本义是里面没有东西的空间。

branches.en: The adjective turns into the act of clearing.
branches.cn: 形容词转化为清空的动作。

branches.en: The container image extends to hollow words and feelings.
branches.cn: 容器意象延伸到空洞的言语与情感。

branches.en: Adjective and verb describe the same missing contents.
branches.cn: 形容词与动词描述同样缺失的内容。

branches.en: Physical emptiness becomes emotional emptiness.
branches.cn: 物理的空变成情感的空。

intro.en: Empty is a native English adjective that also works as a verb.
intro.cn: empty 是英语本族形容词，同时也作动词使用。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in empty; the word is Germanic in origin.
latinIntro.cn: empty 没有拉丁成分，这个词源自日耳曼语。

items.exampleCN: emptying 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: Full is the opposite of empty.
items.exampleCN: full 是 empty 的反义。

items.example: A vacant seat is empty of people.
To clear a room is to empty it.
items.exampleCN: clear a room 就是把房间清空。

definition_zh: 使能够；使成为可能；启用
definition_en: to make someone able to do something, or to make something possible
core_image: 一把钥匙打开平时推不开的门
scene: 这台新机器让我们能更快完成工作。The new machine enables us to work faster.
sceneCN: 这里 enable 是「使能够」（第 1 个义项：使某人有能力做某事）；句意：这台新机器让我们能更快完成工作。

pos.zh: 使能够；使成为可能；启用

senses.title: To make someone able
senses.definition: to give someone the means or ability to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做某事的手段或能力
senses.example: The scholarship enabled her to study abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金使她能够出国留学。
senses.why: The prefix en- puts ability into the person, so the word names the removal of a limit.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 把能力放入一个人身上，因此这个词命名限制的解除。

senses.title: To make something possible
senses.definition: to create the conditions in which an event or process can happen
senses.definitionCN: 创造使某个事件或过程得以发生的条件
senses.example: Good roads enable trade.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的道路使贸易成为可能。
senses.why: Conditions act like keys, so the word also covers making events possible.
senses.whyCN: 条件就像钥匙，因此这个词也涵盖让事件成为可能。

senses.title: To switch a function on
senses.definition: to turn on a feature or setting in a device or program
senses.definitionCN: 打开设备或程序中的某项功能或设置
senses.example: Enable the timer before you start.
senses.exampleCN: 开始前请启用计时器。
senses.why: A feature that is off cannot act, so switching it on is a technical kind of enabling.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的功能无法发挥作用，因此打开它也是一种技术意义上的使能。

intro.en: Enable joins the prefix en-, meaning to make, with the adjective able.
intro.cn: enable 把表示「使成为」的前缀 en- 与形容词 able 结合。

items.en: Habilis means easy to handle or suitable.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌控或合适的。

items.en: Able arrives in English through French, meaning capable.
items.cn: able 经法语进入英语，意为有能力的。

items.en: The prefix en- forms verbs meaning to make or put into.
items.cn: 前缀 en- 构成表示「使成为」的动词。

items.en: Enable appears with the sense of making someone capable.
items.cn: enable 出现，表示使某人有能力。

items.en: The word extends to software settings and social conditions.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词扩展到软件设置与社会条件。

note.en: Enable makes something possible; allow gives permission, and empower adds power or confidence.
note.cn: enable 使成为可能，allow 给予许可，empower 赋予权力或信心。

entries.definition: a person or thing that makes something possible

normalIntro.en: Enable puts ability into a person or situation, so action becomes possible.
normalIntro.cn: enable 把能力放入人或情境中，使行动成为可能。

normal.en: A scholarship enabled her to study.

normal.cn: 词尾 -able 意为有能力的。

abstract.en: Picture a key turning in a stubborn lock.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在卡住的锁里转动。

abstract.en: See a bridge joining two separate banks.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥连接两岸。

abstract.en: Think of a switch that wakes a machine.
abstract.cn: 想象一个唤醒机器的开关。

examples.en: The scholarship enabled her to study abroad.
examples.cn: 奖学金使她能够出国留学。

examples.en: Good roads enable trade.
examples.cn: 良好的道路使贸易成为可能。

examples.en: Enable the timer before you start.
examples.cn: 开始前请启用计时器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因内波」——让事情从「能不能」变成「能」；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 前缀 en-（使成为）+ 形容词 able（有能力的），able 源自拉丁语 habilis。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers giving ability, creating conditions, and switching on a function.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖给予能力、创造条件，以及打开功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key opening a door that was stuck.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙打开卡住的门。

branches.en: The base sense is giving a person ability.
branches.cn: 基本义是给予一个人能力。

branches.en: Conditions can also make events possible.
branches.cn: 条件也能让事件成为可能。

branches.en: A switched-on feature is enabled in a technical sense.
branches.cn: 打开的功能在技术意义上被启用。

branches.en: Personal ability and outward conditions work together.
branches.cn: 个人能力与外在条件共同作用。

branches.en: Tools create the conditions for action.
branches.cn: 工具为行动创造条件。

intro.en: Enable is en- plus able: to make someone able.
intro.cn: enable 是 en- 加 able：使人有能力。

latinIntro.en: Able comes from Latin habilis, meaning suitable or easy to use, through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: able 经古法语来自拉丁语 habilis，意为合适、易于使用。

items.example: The prefix en- makes a verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 构成动词。

items.example: Able is the heart of enable.
items.exampleCN: able 是 enable 的核心。
enabling 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: Enabler names the person who enables.

items.exampleCN: ability 是 enable 所给予的。

definition_en: to surround something with a boundary, or to put something inside an envelope or container
core_image: 木栅栏把花园围成一个安稳的小世界
scene: 农场用木栅栏围住羊群。The farm encloses the sheep with a wooden fence.
sceneCN: 这里 enclose 是「围住」（第 1 个义项：用边界把某物围起来）；句意：农场用木栅栏围住羊群。

senses.title: To surround with a boundary
senses.definition: to put a wall, fence, or other boundary around an area
senses.definitionCN: 用墙、栅栏或其他边界把一片区域围起来
senses.example: A fence encloses the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一道栅栏把花园围了起来。
senses.why: The prefix en- suggests putting something inside, and a boundary keeps it there.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 暗示把某物放入其中，而边界把它留在里面。

senses.title: To put something inside an envelope
senses.definition: to include something inside a letter or package
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放入信件或包裹中一起寄出
senses.example: Please enclose a copy of your passport.
senses.exampleCN: 请随信附上护照复印件。
senses.why: A letter is a container in transit, so putting a document inside is a form of enclosing.
senses.whyCN: 信件是运输中的容器，因此把文件放进去就是一种封入。

senses.title: To contain or seal something in
senses.definition: to shut something inside a container or space
senses.definitionCN: 把某物关在容器或空间内部
senses.example: The seeds are enclosed in a hard shell.
senses.exampleCN: 种子被封在坚硬的壳里。
senses.why: The core idea is being inside a boundary, whether fence, envelope, or shell.
senses.whyCN: 核心概念是被边界包在里面，无论是栅栏、信封还是外壳。

intro.en: Enclose comes from Old French enclore, built on the Latin root claudere, to shut.
intro.cn: enclose 来自古法语 enclore，建立在拉丁词根 claudere（关闭）之上。

items.en: Claudere means to shut or close.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭。

items.en: Enclore means to shut in or surround.
items.cn: enclore 意为关在里面、围住。

items.en: English borrows the verb as enclose or inclose.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 enclose 或 inclose。

items.en: The spelling enclose becomes standard.
items.cn: 拼写 enclose 成为标准。

items.en: The word covers fences, envelopes, and sealed spaces.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词涵盖栅栏、信封和封闭空间。

note.en: Enclose surrounds or seals in; surround is wider, and attach means adding something to a message.
note.cn: enclose 围住或封入，surround 范围更广，attach 指把某物附加到消息中。

entries.definitionCN: 围住；附上（第三人称单数）

entries.definition: an enclosed area or an item sent with a letter
to join something to a message or file

normalIntro.en: Enclose means to put something inside a boundary, an envelope, or a shell.
normalIntro.cn: enclose 意为把某物放入边界、信封或外壳之中。

normal.en: The seeds are enclosed in a shell.
An enclosure is an enclosed space.
normal.cn: enclosure 是被围起来的空间。
被围住的花园是私人的。

abstract.en: Picture a fence drawing a circle around green grass.
abstract.cn: 想象栅栏在绿草周围画出一个圈。

abstract.en: See a letter folded around a small photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象信纸包住一张小照片。

abstract.en: Think of a seed sleeping inside a hard shell.
abstract.cn: 想象种子睡在坚硬的外壳里。

examples.en: A fence encloses the garden.
examples.cn: 一道栅栏把花园围了起来。

examples.en: Please enclose a copy of your passport.
examples.cn: 请随信附上护照复印件。

examples.en: The seeds are enclosed in a hard shell.
examples.cn: 种子被封在坚硬的壳里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因克洛斯」——把东西「克」制在里面、关起来；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 enclore，建立在拉丁语 claudere（关闭）的词根上。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers boundaries, items sent in letters, and spaces sealed by shells or walls.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖边界、随信附上的物品，以及被外壳或墙壁封闭的空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fence making a safe circle on open ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：栅栏在空地上围出安全的圆圈。

branches.en: The base sense is surrounding an area with a boundary.
branches.cn: 基本义是用边界围住一片区域。

branches.en: A letter becomes a container for an enclosed item.
branches.cn: 信件成为所附物品的容器。

branches.en: Any boundary that seals something inside fits the image.
branches.cn: 任何把东西封在里面的边界都符合这一意象。

branches.en: Fences and shells both keep an inside apart.
branches.cn: 栅栏与外壳都把内部隔开。

branches.en: The envelope and the shell are both enclosures.
branches.cn: 信封与外壳都是封闭物。

intro.en: Enclose joins en-, meaning in, with the Latin root claud, meaning to shut.
intro.cn: enclose 把意为「在内」的 en- 与意为关闭的拉丁词根 claud 结合。

latinIntro.en: The root claudere, to shut, also appears in include and exclude.
latinIntro.cn: 意为关闭的词根 claudere 也出现在 include 与 exclude 中。

items.example: The prefix en- puts something inside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 把某物放入其中。

items.example: The root claud- hides inside enclose.
items.exampleCN: 词根 claud- 藏在 enclose 里。
enclosing 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: Include also means to shut in.
Exclude is the opposite of include.
items.exampleCN: exclude 是 include 的反面。

items.example: Close and enclose share one idea.
items.exampleCN: close 与 enclose 共享一个概念。

definition_en: to meet someone or face something unexpectedly
core_image: 转过林间小路，突然与一只鹿面对面
scene: 我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。We encountered a deer in the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 encounter 是「遇到」（第 1 个义项：意外遇见某人或某物）；句意：我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。

senses.title: To meet someone or something
senses.definition: to meet a person, animal, or thing, especially by chance
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指偶然遇见某人、动物或事物
senses.example: We encountered a deer in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。
senses.why: The word is built on a Latin phrase for coming face to face, so it stresses the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「面对面」的说法上，因此强调相遇本身。

senses.title: To face a difficulty
senses.definition: to experience or come up against a problem, danger, or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 经历或直面问题、危险或反对
senses.example: The team encountered several problems.
senses.exampleCN: 团队遇到了几个问题。
senses.why: A difficulty stands in one's path like a person, so meeting it becomes encountering it.
senses.whyCN: 困难像人一样挡在路上，因此与它相遇就变成遭遇它。

senses.title: A meeting or confrontation
senses.definition: an unexpected meeting or a short conflict between people
senses.definitionCN: 意外的会面或人与人之间短暂的交锋
senses.example: Their first encounter was brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的初次相遇很短暂。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun naming the event of coming face to face.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，命名面对面相遇的事件。

intro.en: Encounter comes from Old French encontrer, from Latin phrases meaning in the face of.
intro.cn: encounter 来自古法语 encontrer，源于拉丁语中意为「面对」的说法。

items.en: In contrā means against or facing.

items.en: The noun appears for meetings and clashes.

note.en: Encounter is often unexpected; meet is neutral, and face stresses dealing with a problem.

examples.cn: 我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers chance meetings, facing difficulties, and the event of a clash.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖偶遇、面对困难，以及交锋事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coming face to face on a forest path.
core.cn: 核心意象：在林间小路上面对面。

branches.en: The base sense is meeting someone or something.
branches.cn: 基本义是遇见某人或某物。

branches.en: Difficulties can be met as if they were opponents.
branches.cn: 困难可以像对手一样被遭遇。

branches.en: The verb also names the event itself.
branches.cn: 动词也命名事件本身。

branches.en: Meeting and the meeting are one idea in two forms.
branches.cn: 相遇与相遇事件是同一概念的两个形式。

branches.en: A clash is a meeting that turns hostile.
branches.cn: 交锋是变成敌对的相遇。

intro.en: Encounter contains the Latin element contra, meaning against or facing.
intro.cn: encounter 含有拉丁成分 contra，意为相对、面对。

latinIntro.en: Contra, against, also appears in contrast and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 意为相对的 contra 也出现在 contrast 与 contradict 中。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 开启 encounter。

items.example: Contra is the heart of encounter.
items.exampleCN: contra 是 encounter 的核心。
encountering 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: To encounter is to meet unexpectedly.

items.meaning: to look toward or deal with

definition_en: to give someone confidence or support to do something, or to help something grow
core_image: 老师拍拍学生的肩，让他再试一次
scene: 老师鼓励我们大胆提问。Our teacher encourages us to ask questions.
sceneCN: 这里 encourage 是「鼓励」（第 1 个义项：给某人信心或支持去做某事）；句意：老师鼓励我们大胆提问。

senses.title: To give someone confidence
senses.definition: to give a person support, hope, or confidence to do something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人支持、希望或信心去做某事
senses.example: Our teacher encourages us to ask questions.
senses.exampleCN: 老师鼓励我们大胆提问。
senses.why: The word contains courage, so encouraging is putting heart into someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词含有 courage，因此鼓励就是把勇气放进别人心里。

senses.title: To help something develop
senses.definition: to make an activity, condition, or growth more likely
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动、状况或增长更有可能发生
senses.example: Warm weather encourages plant growth.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的天气促进植物生长。
senses.why: Support can be given to processes as well as people, so the word also means fostering.
senses.whyCN: 支持不仅能给人，也能给过程，因此这个词也指培育促进。

senses.title: To urge or recommend
senses.definition: to suggest strongly that someone should do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈建议某人应该做某事
senses.example: Doctors encourage regular exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 医生提倡规律运动。
senses.why: Encouragement often includes advice, so the word can carry a gentle push toward action.
senses.whyCN: 鼓励常包含建议，因此这个词也带有温和推动行动的意味。

intro.en: Encourage comes from Old French encoragier, to put courage into someone.
intro.cn: encourage 来自古法语 encoragier，意为把勇气放进某人心里。

items.en: Cor means heart, the source of courage.
items.cn: cor 意为心，是勇气的来源。

items.en: Corage means courage, and encoragier means to strengthen it.
items.cn: corage 意为勇气，encoragier 意为增强勇气。

items.en: English borrows the verb as encourage.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，写作 encourage。

items.en: The word widens to mean supporting any action or growth.
items.cn: 在近代早期，词义扩展到支持任何行动或成长。

items.en: Encourage covers confidence, development, and gentle urging.
items.cn: 现代英语中，encourage 涵盖信心、发展和温和劝导。

note.en: Encourage gives confidence; support is broader, motivate supplies a reason, and inspire stirs the heart.
note.cn: encourage 给予信心，support 范围更广，motivate 提供理由，inspire 激发内心。

entries.definition: support or confidence given to someone
to give someone a reason to act
to fill someone with strong feeling or ideas

sensesIntro.en: The word covers giving confidence, fostering growth, and urging a course of action.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖给予信心、促进成长，以及劝导采取行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: courage placed into another person's heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：把勇气放进另一个人的心里。

branches.en: The base sense is giving confidence to a person.
branches.cn: 基本义是给一个人信心。

branches.en: People and living things both respond to support.

branches.en: Fostering often takes the form of advice.

intro.en: Encourage is en- plus courage, the old word for heart-based bravery.
intro.cn: encourage 是 en- 加 courage，即源于内心的勇气。

latinIntro.en: Courage descends from Latin cor, heart, through Old French corage.
latinIntro.cn: courage 经古法语 corage 来自拉丁语 cor（心）。

items.example: The prefix en- puts courage in.

definition_zh: 鼓励；激励；起鼓励作用的事物
definition_en: the act of giving someone confidence, or something that gives hope
core_image: 一张写着「再试一次」的小纸条，被悄悄塞进课本
scene: 掌声给了她继续表演的鼓励。The applause gave her encouragement to continue.
sceneCN: 这里 encouragement 是「鼓励」（第 1 个义项：给予信心和支持的行为）；句意：掌声给了她继续表演的鼓励。

senses.title: The act of giving confidence
senses.definition: the act of giving someone support, hope, or confidence
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人支持、希望或信心的行为
senses.example: Her encouragement helped me finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她的鼓励帮我跑完了比赛。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb gives, so encouragement is support passed from one person to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名动词所给予的东西，因此鼓励是从一个人传给另一个人的支持。

senses.title: Something that gives hope
senses.definition: a word, action, or event that makes someone feel more hopeful
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到更有希望的言语、行动或事件
senses.example: The letter was a great encouragement.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信是极大的鼓励。
senses.why: Support can be counted as a thing, so a kind message becomes an encouragement.
senses.whyCN: 支持可以被当作具体事物来计数，因此一句善意的话就成了一份鼓励。

intro.en: Encouragement is encourage plus -ment, naming the support that is given.
intro.cn: encouragement 是 encourage 加 -ment，命名所给予的支持。

items.en: Cor, heart, is the root of courage.
items.cn: cor（心）是 courage 的词根。

items.en: Encoragier means to put courage into someone.

items.en: Encourage enters English as a verb.
items.cn: encourage 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The noun encouragement appears for the support given.
items.cn: 名词 encouragement 出现，指给予的支持。

items.en: The word covers both the act and the thing that inspires.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词既指行为，也指鼓舞人的事物。

note.en: Encouragement is support that builds confidence; motivation supplies a reason, and inspiration stirs ideas.
note.cn: encouragement 是建立信心的支持，motivation 提供理由，inspiration 激发想法。

entries.definition: a reason or drive to act
a sudden good idea or strong feeling

normalIntro.cn: encouragement 是用言语或行动递过去的勇气。

normal.en: Words of encouragement help a friend.
Her letter was a great encouragement.

normal.cn: 令人鼓舞的消息提升士气。

examples.cn: 鼓励的话不需要花一分钱。

root: encourage 加名词词尾 -ment，深层词根源自拉丁语 cor（心）。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the act of supporting someone and the message or event that gives hope.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词命名支持他人的行为，以及带来希望的讯息或事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: courage handed over like a small gift.
core.cn: 核心意象：像小礼物一样被递过去的勇气。

branches.en: The base sense is the act of giving support.
branches.cn: 基本义是给予支持的行为。

branches.en: The support can be counted as a message or event.
branches.cn: 这种支持可以具体化为讯息或事件。

branches.en: Act and object both produce confidence.
branches.cn: 行为与事物都产生信心。

branches.en: The -ment ending turns the action into a noun.
branches.cn: 词尾 -ment 把动作变成名词。

intro.cn: encouragement 是 en- 加 courage 再加 -ment，是整个行为的名词形式。

definition_en: the last part of something, the point where it stops, or a purpose
core_image: 小路走到尽头，一棵大树安静地站在那里
scene: 小路的尽头有一棵大树。There is a big tree at the end of the path.
sceneCN: 这里 end 是「尽头」（第 1 个义项：某物最末的一端）；句意：小路的尽头有一棵大树。

senses.title: The last part of something
senses.definition: the furthest or final part of a place or object
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方或物体最远、最末的一端
senses.example: There is a tree at the end of the path.
senses.exampleCN: 小路的尽头有一棵树。
senses.why: A line has a point where it stops, so the word first names that outermost part.
senses.whyCN: 一条线有一个停止的点，因此这个词首先命名最外侧的部分。

senses.title: The point when something stops
senses.definition: the moment or event at which something finishes
senses.definitionCN: 某事完成的时刻或事件
senses.example: The meeting came to an end at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在中午结束。
senses.why: When time runs to its last point, the same image marks completion.
senses.whyCN: 当时间走到最后一点，同一个意象就标记完成。

senses.title: A purpose or goal
senses.definition: the aim or result that someone works toward
senses.definitionCN: 某人努力追求的目标或结果
senses.example: The end of the project is a cleaner river.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的目的是让河流更干净。
senses.why: A journey's endpoint is also its purpose, so end can mean the goal itself.
senses.whyCN: 旅程的终点也是它的目的，因此 end 可以指目标本身。

intro.en: End is an old Germanic word for a boundary or outermost point.
intro.cn: end 是古老的日耳曼词，意为边界或最外端的点。

items.en: The ancestor word refers to a boundary or edge.
items.cn: 祖语词指边界或边缘。

items.en: End means a boundary, a conclusion, or a purpose.
items.cn: end 意为边界、结论或目的。

items.en: The word keeps all three senses in everyday use.
items.cn: 这个词在日常使用中保留三种含义。

items.en: End becomes common in phrases about time and goals.
items.cn: 在近代早期，end 常见于关于时间与目标的短语中。

items.en: End works as a noun and a verb.
items.cn: 现代英语中，end 兼作名词与动词。

note.en: End is the last point; finish stresses completion, and goal stresses purpose.
note.cn: end 是最末一点，finish 强调完成，goal 强调目的。

entries.definition: the final part of a story or word

normalIntro.en: End is where something stops, whether a path, a meeting, or a plan.
normalIntro.cn: end 是某物停止之处，无论是一条路、一次会议还是一个计划。

normal.en: The tree stands at the end.
The end can also mean the goal.

abstract.en: Picture a road narrowing to a single point.
abstract.cn: 想象道路收窄成一个点。

abstract.en: See a clock hand reaching the final mark.
abstract.cn: 想象钟针走到最后刻度。

abstract.en: Think of a finish line painted on the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象画在地上的终点线。

examples.en: The end of the project is a cleaner river.

sensesIntro.en: The word covers the outermost point, the moment of completion, and the purpose of an action.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖最外的端点、完成的时刻，以及行动的目的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a path reaching its final tree.
core.cn: 核心意象：小路走到最后一棵树。

branches.en: The base sense is the furthest part of a thing.
branches.cn: 基本义是事物最远的部分。

branches.en: The final point in time becomes completion.
branches.cn: 时间上的最后一点变成完成。

branches.en: The endpoint of effort becomes its purpose.
branches.cn: 努力的终点变成它的目的。

branches.en: Space and time share the image of a last point.

branches.en: Finishing is reaching the goal one aimed at.

intro.en: End is a short native root that builds endings, endless, and endpoint.
intro.cn: end 是简短的本族词根，可构成 ending、endless 与 endpoint。

definition_en: having no end, or seeming to continue for too long

scene: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。The desert looked endless in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 endless 是「无边无际的」（第 1 个义项：似乎没有尽头）；句意：沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。

senses.title: Having no visible end
senses.definition: seeming to have no limit in space or time
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上似乎没有边界
senses.example: The desert looked endless in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。
senses.why: The suffix -less removes the end, so the word pictures something stretching beyond sight.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -less 去掉了尽头，因此这个词描绘延伸到视野之外的事物。

senses.title: Tiringly long
senses.definition: continuing so long that it feels boring or exhausting
senses.definitionCN: 持续太久以致令人厌烦或疲惫
senses.example: The meeting felt endless.
senses.exampleCN: 会议感觉没完没了。
senses.why: What has no end in sight can wear a person down, so the word also carries impatience.
senses.whyCN: 看不到终点的事物会消耗人，因此这个词也带不耐烦的意味。

intro.en: Endless is end plus the old suffix -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: endless 是 end 加古老词尾 -less，意为没有。

items.en: Endeleas already means without end.
items.cn: 古英语 endelēas 已意为没有尽头。

items.en: The spelling settles as endless.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 endless。

items.en: Endless describes long roads, waits, and speeches.
items.cn: 在近代早期，endless 描述漫长的道路、等待与讲话。

items.en: The word gains the sense of tediously long.
items.cn: 这个词获得冗长烦人的含义。

items.en: Endless often appears in phrases about possibilities and delays.
items.cn: 当代英语中，endless 常用于可能性和拖延的表述。

note.en: Endless means no end in sight; infinite is more exact, and nonstop means without pause.
note.cn: endless 指看不到尽头，infinite 更精确，nonstop 指不停顿。

normalIntro.en: Endless is end plus -less: an end taken away, so the road runs on.
normalIntro.cn: endless 是 end 加 -less：去掉了尽头，所以路一直延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a road meeting a flat horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象道路与平坦地平线相接。

abstract.en: See a queue that never moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条始终不动的队伍。

abstract.en: Think of waves repeating on a dark sea.
abstract.cn: 想象暗色海面上重复的波浪。

examples.en: The desert looked endless in the heat.
examples.cn: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。

examples.en: The meeting felt endless.
examples.cn: 会议感觉没完没了。

examples.en: Endless possibilities lie ahead.
examples.cn: 前方有无限可能。

root: 古英语 endelēas，由 end（尽头）加 -less（没有）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers space or time without a visible limit, and duration that wears patience thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖看不到边界的空间或时间，以及消磨耐心的漫长持续。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road running beyond the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：延伸到地平线之外的道路。

branches.en: The base sense is having no visible limit.
branches.cn: 基本义是看不到界限。

branches.en: Too much length in time becomes weariness.
branches.cn: 时间上的过长变成疲惫。

branches.en: A space without end and a wait without end share one shape.
branches.cn: 无边的空间与无尽的等待共享同一种形状。

branches.en: The -less suffix removes the boundary.
branches.cn: 词尾 -less 移除了边界。

branches.en: Endless tasks make people sigh.
branches.cn: 没完没了的任务让人叹气。

intro.en: Endless is end plus -less, the suffix for lacking something.
intro.cn: endless 是 end 加 -less，即表示缺乏某物的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Endless is purely Germanic; Latin-based synonyms include infinite.
latinIntro.cn: endless 纯属日耳曼来源，拉丁来源的近义词是 infinite。

items.example: End is the base of endless.
items.exampleCN: end 是 endless 的基础。
infinite 是拉丁来源的近义词。

definition_en: to suffer something difficult patiently, or to continue to exist for a long time
core_image: 暴风雪里，一棵老树弯下腰却没有折断
scene: 她忍受了漫长而寒冷的冬天。She endured the long, cold winter.
sceneCN: 这里 endure 是「忍受」（第 1 个义项：耐心承受痛苦或困难）；句意：她忍受了漫长而寒冷的冬天。

senses.title: To bear something difficult
senses.definition: to suffer pain, hardship, or an unpleasant situation patiently
senses.definitionCN: 耐心承受疼痛、艰苦或不愉快的处境
senses.example: She endured the long, cold winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她忍受了漫长而寒冷的冬天。
senses.why: The Latin root means to harden, so enduring is standing firm under pressure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为变硬，因此忍受就是在压力下站稳。

senses.title: To last or continue
senses.definition: to continue to exist or remain strong over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间继续存在或保持稳固
senses.example: The old bridge has endured for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老桥已经屹立了几个世纪。
senses.why: What hardens against wear can also last, so the word shifts from bearing to surviving.
senses.whyCN: 能抗住磨损的事物也能长久存在，因此词义从承受转向存续。

intro.en: Endure comes from Latin indurare, to harden, through Old French endurer.
intro.cn: endure 来自拉丁语 indurare（使变硬），经古法语 endurer 进入英语。

items.en: Indurare means to make hard or to last.
items.cn: indurare 意为使变硬、持续。

items.en: Endurer means to bear or suffer.
items.cn: endurer 意为承受、忍受。

items.en: English borrows endure with both bearing and lasting senses.
items.cn: 英语借入 endure，兼具忍受与持续两义。

items.en: Endure becomes common for pain, hardship, and time.
items.cn: 在近代早期，endure 常用于疼痛、艰苦与时间。

items.en: The word still joins patient suffering with lasting strength.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词仍把耐心承受与持久力量结合在一起。

note.en: Endure bears pain over time; tolerate is more neutral, and last stresses continuing to exist.
note.cn: endure 长期承受痛苦，tolerate 更中性，last 强调继续存在。

entries.definition: to accept something unpleasant without protest

normalIntro.en: Endure is to harden yourself under pain and to keep standing over time.
normalIntro.cn: endure 是在痛苦中让自己变硬，并随时间继续站立。

normal.en: The bridge has endured for centuries.
normal.cn: 这座桥屹立了几个世纪。

normal.en: Endurance is the ability to endure.
Enduring value lasts a long time.
Some pain is hard to endure.

abstract.cn: 想象老树在暴风雪中弯腰。

abstract.en: See a stone bridge worn smooth by time.
abstract.cn: 想象被时间磨得光滑的石桥。

abstract.en: Think of a rope holding under heavy weight.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子在重压下坚持。

examples.cn: 她忍受了漫长而寒冷的冬天。

examples.en: The old bridge has endured for centuries.
examples.cn: 这座老桥已经屹立了几个世纪。

examples.en: Some pain is hard to endure.
examples.cn: 有些痛苦难以忍受。

root: 拉丁语 indurare（使变硬），经古法语 endurer 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers bearing hardship patiently and continuing to exist over time.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖耐心承受艰苦，以及随时间继续存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old tree bending but not breaking in a storm.
core.cn: 核心意象：老树在暴风雪中弯曲却不断。

branches.en: The base sense is bearing pain or hardship.
branches.cn: 基本义是承受痛苦或艰苦。

branches.en: What bears wear also continues to exist.
branches.cn: 能承受磨损的事物也继续存在。

branches.en: Patience and durability grow from the same hardness.
branches.cn: 耐心与耐久来自同一种坚硬。

branches.en: The -ance noun names the strength to bear.
branches.cn: -ance 名词命名承受的力量。

branches.en: Enduring things outlast their makers.
branches.cn: 持久的事物比制造者活得更久。

intro.en: Endure is built on the Latin root dur, meaning hard or lasting.
intro.cn: endure 建立在拉丁词根 dur 上，意为坚硬、持久。

latinIntro.en: Durare, to last, also gives durable and duration.
latinIntro.cn: durare（持续）也构成 durable 与 duration。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 进入 endure。

items.example: The root dur- hides inside endure.
items.exampleCN: 词根 dur- 藏在 endure 里。

items.example: To endure is to become hard.

definition_en: a person or group that is hostile to another, or something harmful
core_image: 两位骑士隔着河流对峙，谁也不肯先低头
scene: 在故事里，骑士与他的敌人隔河相望。In the story the knight and his enemy faced each other across the river.
sceneCN: 这里 enemy 是「敌人」（第 1 个义项：怀有敌意、与之对抗的人）；句意：在故事里，骑士与他的敌人隔河相望。

senses.title: A hostile person
senses.definition: a person who is strongly opposed to another and wishes them harm
senses.definitionCN: 强烈反对他人并希望其受到伤害的人
senses.example: The knight faced his enemy across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 骑士隔着河面对他的敌人。
senses.why: The Latin original means not a friend, so the word begins as the direct opposite of friend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原词意为「不是朋友」，因此这个词起初就是朋友的直接反面。

senses.title: An opposing army or group
senses.definition: the military force or group that one is fighting against
senses.definitionCN: 正在与之作战的军队或团体
senses.example: The enemy advanced at night.
senses.exampleCN: 敌军在夜里推进。
senses.why: Individual hostility grows into organized conflict, so the word also names the opposing side.
senses.whyCN: 个人的敌意发展成有组织的冲突，因此这个词也指对立的一方。

senses.title: Something harmful
senses.definition: a thing that harms or threatens something valued
senses.definitionCN: 损害或威胁有价值之物的东西
senses.example: Disease is the enemy of a good harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 病害是丰收的大敌。
senses.why: Anything that attacks a goal acts like an opponent, so the word extends to harmful forces.
senses.whyCN: 任何攻击目标的事物都像对手，因此这个词扩展到有害的力量。

intro.en: Enemy comes from Latin inimicus, literally not a friend.
intro.cn: enemy 来自拉丁语 inimicus，字面意思是「不是朋友」。

items.en: Inimicus joins in-, not, with amicus, friend.
items.cn: inimicus 把否定的 in- 与 amicus（朋友）结合。

items.en: The word becomes enemi in French.
items.cn: 这个词在法语中写作 enemi。

items.en: English borrows it as enemy.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 enemy。

items.en: Enemy covers both personal foes and opposing armies.
items.cn: 在近代早期，enemy 既指个人仇敌，也指敌对军队。

items.en: The word also names impersonal threats such as disease.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词也命名疾病等非人的威胁。

note.en: An enemy is hostile; an opponent competes, a rival seeks the same goal, and a foe is a literary enemy.
note.cn: enemy 怀有敌意，opponent 竞争，rival 争夺同一目标，foe 是文学化的敌人。

entries.definition: a person competing for the same thing
an enemy, used in formal or literary writing

normalIntro.en: An enemy is literally a not-friend, and the word extends to armies and threats.
normalIntro.cn: enemy 字面上是「不是朋友」，词义扩展到军队与威胁。

normal.en: Disease is an enemy of crops.

normal.cn: 共同的敌人让人们团结。

normal.en: Enmity is the feeling between enemies.
normal.cn: enmity 是敌人之间的敌意。

abstract.cn: 想象河两岸对立的两个身影。

abstract.en: See a wall built between two gardens.
abstract.cn: 想象两座花园之间筑起的墙。

abstract.en: Think of rust quietly eating iron.
abstract.cn: 想象锈悄悄侵蚀铁。

examples.cn: 骑士隔着河面对他的敌人。

examples.cn: 敌军在夜里推进。

examples.en: Disease is the enemy of a good harvest.
examples.cn: 病害是丰收的大敌。

root: 拉丁语 inimicus，由 in-（非）+ amicus（朋友）构成，经古法语 enemi 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a hostile person, an opposing force, and anything that threatens a goal.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词命名怀有敌意的人、对立的力量，以及任何威胁目标的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rivals facing each other across a river.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个对手隔河对峙。

branches.en: The base sense is a hostile person.
branches.cn: 基本义是怀有敌意的人。

branches.en: Personal hostility grows into an opposing army.
branches.cn: 个人敌意发展成敌对军队。

branches.en: Anything that attacks a goal acts as an enemy.
branches.cn: 任何攻击目标的事物都充当敌人。

branches.en: One person and one army share the same hostility.
branches.cn: 一个人和一支军队共享同样的敌意。

branches.en: Both organized and natural threats must be fought.
branches.cn: 有组织的威胁与自然的威胁都必须对抗。

intro.en: Enemy is built from the Latin negative in- and amicus, friend.
intro.cn: enemy 由拉丁否定前缀 in- 与 amicus（朋友）构成。

latinIntro.en: Inimicus, not a friend, is the direct Latin source of enemy.
latinIntro.cn: inimicus（不是朋友）是 enemy 的直接拉丁来源。

items.exampleCN: in- 把朋友变成非朋友。
词根 amic- 意为朋友。

items.example: An enemy is not a friend.
Foe is an old word for enemy.
items.exampleCN: foe 是 enemy 的古老说法。

items.example: A rival is less hostile than an enemy.

items.example: The enemy army crossed the river.

definition_en: the strength to be active, or the power that makes things work
core_image: 清晨的阳光照进花园，花草仿佛一下子有了劲儿
scene: 早晨的阳光给花园带来温暖的能量。The morning sun brings warm energy to the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 energy 是「能量」（第 1 个义项：使事物运作或生长的力量）；句意：早晨的阳光给花园带来温暖的能量。

senses.title: Physical or mental strength
senses.definition: the strength and liveliness that let a person act or think
senses.definitionCN: 使人能够行动或思考的体力与活力
senses.example: The children are full of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们精力充沛。
senses.why: The word begins with the idea of work being done, so in a person it appears as the power to act.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指工作被完成，因此在人身上表现为行动的力量。

senses.title: Power in physics
senses.definition: the capacity of a system to do work, studied in physics
senses.definitionCN: 系统做功的能力，是物理学的研究对象
senses.example: Heat is a form of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 热是一种能量。
senses.why: Science takes the everyday sense of power and makes it a measurable quantity.
senses.whyCN: 科学把日常的力量概念变成可测量的量。

senses.title: Resources such as fuel or electricity
senses.definition: resources used to produce heat, light, or motion
senses.definitionCN: 用来产生热、光或运动的资源
senses.example: Solar energy is clean.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳能是清洁的。
senses.why: Fuel stores the power that machines need, so the word also names the supply itself.
senses.whyCN: 燃料储存机器所需的动力，因此这个词也命名供应来源本身。

intro.en: Energy comes from Greek energeia, meaning activity or working.
intro.cn: energy 来自希腊语 energeia，意为活动、运作。

items.en: Energeia means activity or actual work.
items.cn: energeia 意为活动或实际运作。

items.en: The word enters Latin as energia.
items.cn: 这个词以 energia 进入拉丁语。

items.en: English borrows energy for force and vigour.
items.cn: 十七世纪，英语借入 energy，表示力量与活力。

items.en: Physics gives energy its precise scientific sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪，物理学赋予 energy 精确的科学含义。

items.en: Energy now covers personal vigour, physics, and fuel supplies.
items.cn: 现代英语中，energy 涵盖个人精力、物理能量与能源供应。

note.en: Energy is the power to act; strength is muscular force, and power is the rate of doing work.
note.cn: energy 是行动的力量，strength 是肌肉力量，power 是做功的速率。

entries.definition: the powers or efforts of a person or group

normalIntro.en: Energy is the power to work, whether in a body, a machine, or a fuel.

normal.en: Heat is a form of energy.

normal.cn: 精力充沛的人行动迅速。

root: 希腊语 energeia（活动、运作），经拉丁语 energia 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers personal vigour, the physical quantity of work, and the fuels that supply power.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖个人精力、物理上的功，以及提供动力的燃料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight pouring power into living leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光把力量注入活着的叶片。

branches.en: The base sense is a person's power to act.
branches.cn: 基本义是一个人行动的力量。

branches.en: Physics measures the same power as energy.
branches.cn: 物理学把同一种力量测量为能量。

branches.en: Fuels are the supplies that carry energy.
branches.cn: 燃料是携带能量的供应来源。

branches.en: A lively body and a working machine share one idea.
branches.cn: 有活力的身体与运转的机器共享一个概念。

branches.en: Stored energy becomes useful power.
branches.cn: 储存的能量变成有用的动力。

intro.en: Energy is built on the Greek root erg, meaning work.
intro.cn: energy 建立在希腊词根 erg 上，意为工作。

latinIntro.en: The Greek word energeia passed into Latin as energia before reaching English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词 energeia 以 energia 进入拉丁语，再进入英语。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 开启 energy。
词根 erg- 意为工作。

items.example: Energy and power are close ideas.
items.exampleCN: energy 与 power 概念相近。

definition_zh: 执行；强制实施；迫使服从
definition_en: to make people obey a law or rule, often by using authority
core_image: 交警站在路口，确保每辆车都遵守信号灯
scene: 警察负责执行交通规则。The police enforce traffic rules.
sceneCN: 这里 enforce 是「执行」（第 1 个义项：用权威确保人们遵守规则）；句意：警察负责执行交通规则。

senses.title: To make a law or rule obeyed
senses.definition: to make sure that a law or rule is obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 确保法律或规则被遵守
senses.example: The police enforce traffic rules.
senses.exampleCN: 警察负责执行交通规则。
senses.why: The prefix en- adds force, so the word means putting force behind a rule so it is not merely written.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 en- 加上力量，因此这个词意为给规则加力，使它不只是写在纸上。

senses.title: To force people to accept something
senses.definition: to make people accept or follow something by authority or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过权威或压力使人们接受或遵守某事
senses.example: The school enforces a strict dress code.
senses.exampleCN: 学校强制执行严格的着装规定。
senses.why: Enforcement can involve pressure, so the word also covers forcing compliance.
senses.whyCN: 执行可能涉及压力，因此这个词也涵盖强迫服从。

senses.title: To give strength to a claim or rule
senses.definition: to make an argument, right, or condition stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使论点、权利或条件更有力、更有效
senses.example: The new evidence enforces their claim.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据使他们的主张更有力。
senses.why: To enforce is to add force, so a claim can be strengthened as a rule can be upheld.
senses.whyCN: enforce 就是加力，因此主张能像规则一样被加强。

intro.en: Enforce comes from Old French enforcier, to give force to something.
intro.cn: enforce 来自古法语 enforcier，意为给某物加力。

items.en: Fortis means strong, the root behind force.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮，是 force 背后的词根。

items.en: Enforcier means to strengthen or compel.
items.cn: enforcier 意为加强或强迫。

items.en: English borrows enforce with the sense of giving force.
items.cn: 英语借入 enforce，表示施加力量。

items.en: The legal sense of carrying out laws becomes common.
items.cn: 在近代早期，执行法律的义项变得常见。

items.en: Enforce now chiefly means making rules obeyed.
items.cn: 现代英语中，enforce 主要指使规则被遵守。

note.en: Enforce makes rules obeyed; implement puts plans into action, and impose forces something on people.
note.cn: enforce 使规则被遵守，implement 把计划付诸行动，impose 把某物强加于人。

to use a rule in a situation

normalIntro.en: Enforce means to put force behind a rule so people must follow it.
normalIntro.cn: enforce 意为给规则加力，使人们必须遵守。

normal.en: The school enforces a dress code.

root: 古法语 enforcier（加力），来自拉丁语 fortis（强壮）。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers carrying out laws, forcing compliance, and giving strength to a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖执行法律、强迫服从，以及加强主张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red light obeyed by every car.
core.cn: 核心意象：每辆车都遵守的红灯。

branches.en: The base sense is making a law obeyed.
branches.cn: 基本义是使法律被遵守。

branches.en: Authority can also force acceptance of a rule.

definition_en: to attract and hold attention, to take part in something, or to employ someone
core_image: 故事讲到一半，所有孩子都往前探着身子
scene: 这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。The story engaged the attention of every child.
sceneCN: 这里 engage 是「吸引」（第 1 个义项：抓住并保持注意力）；句意：这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。

senses.title: To attract and hold attention
senses.definition: to attract someone's interest so that they stay involved
senses.definitionCN: 吸引某人的兴趣并使其持续投入
senses.example: The story engaged the attention of every child.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事吸引了所有孩子的注意力。
senses.why: The old sense of pledging oneself survives as giving one's attention fully to something.
senses.whyCN: 古代表明承诺的含义保留下来，表现为把注意力完全交给某事。

senses.title: To take part in an activity
senses.definition: to become involved in an activity or discussion
senses.definitionCN: 参与某项活动或讨论
senses.example: The students engaged in a debate.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们参与了一场辩论。
senses.why: To engage is to commit oneself, so joining an activity is a form of pledge.
senses.whyCN: engage 意为投入自己，因此加入活动是一种承诺形式。

senses.title: To employ or hire someone
senses.definition: to arrange for someone to work for you for a time
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人为你工作一段时间
senses.example: They engaged a lawyer for the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为这个案子聘请了一位律师。
senses.why: Hiring is a formal commitment between two parties, so the pledge sense returns.
senses.whyCN: 雇用是双方之间正式的承诺，因此承诺义又回来了。

intro.en: Engage comes from Old French engagier, to pledge or bind by promise.

items.en: Gage means a pledge, and engagier means to pledge.

items.en: English borrows engage with the sense of pledging oneself.

items.en: The word gains senses of hiring and taking part.
items.cn: 这个词获得雇用与参与的含义。

items.en: Engage becomes common for holding attention.

items.en: The word covers attention, involvement, and employment.

note.en: Engage is to attract or involve; attract pulls interest, and participate means to take part.

definition_zh: 发动机；引擎；火车头；推动力
definition_en: a machine that converts power into motion, or something that drives a process
core_image: 发动机低低地震动，把整辆车推向前方
scene: 汽车发动机发出低低的响声。The car engine made a low sound.
sceneCN: 这里 engine 是「发动机」（第 1 个义项：把动力转化为运动的机器）；句意：汽车发动机发出低低的响声。

pos.zh: 发动机；引擎；火车头；推动力

senses.title: A machine that produces motion
senses.definition: a machine that turns fuel or electricity into movement
senses.definitionCN: 把燃料或电力转化为运动的机器
senses.example: The car engine made a low sound.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车发动机发出低低的响声。
senses.why: The word descends from a term for skill or invention, so the machine is a product of clever design.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自表示技巧或发明的词，因此机器是巧妙设计的产物。

senses.title: A railway locomotive
senses.definition: the part of a train that provides the power to pull it
senses.definitionCN: 火车中提供牵引动力的部分
senses.example: The engine pulled ten carriages.
senses.exampleCN: 火车头拉动了十节车厢。
senses.why: Early locomotives were the most visible engines, so the word became their everyday name.
senses.whyCN: 早期机车是最显眼的发动机，因此这个词成了它们的日常名称。

senses.title: A force that drives a process
senses.definition: something that causes or drives activity, growth, or change
senses.definitionCN: 引起或推动活动、成长或变化的事物
senses.example: Trade is the engine of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易是这座城市的推动力。
senses.why: A machine's engine moves a vehicle, so the image transfers to anything that drives progress.
senses.whyCN: 机器的发动机推动车辆，因此这一意象转移到任何推动进步的事物上。

intro.en: Engine comes from Latin ingenium, natural ability or clever invention.
intro.cn: engine 来自拉丁语 ingenium，意为天赋或巧妙的发明。

items.en: Ingenium means inborn talent or cleverness.

items.en: English borrows engine for a device or invention.

items.en: Steam engines make the machine sense dominant.

items.en: Engine means a motor, a locomotive, or a driving force.

note.en: An engine converts power into motion; a motor is often electric, and a machine is the broader word.
note.cn: engine 把动力转化为运动，motor 常指电动机，machine 是更宽泛的词。

definition_zh: 工程师；设计建造；巧妙安排
definition_en: a person who designs machines or structures, or to plan and build something skillfully
core_image: 工程师伏在图纸上，把一座桥一笔一笔画出来
scene: 这位工程师设计了一座更安全的桥。The engineer designed a safer bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 engineer 是「工程师」（第 1 个义项：设计机器或结构的人）；句意：这位工程师设计了一座更安全的桥。

senses.title: A person who designs machines or structures
senses.definition: a person trained to design, build, or maintain machines, structures, or systems
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、设计、建造或维护机器、结构或系统的人
senses.example: The engineer designed a safer bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这位工程师设计了一座更安全的桥。
senses.why: The suffix -eer marks a person concerned with a field, so an engineer is one who works with engines and designs.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -eer 标记从事某一领域的人，因此 engineer 是与发动机和设计打交道的人。

senses.title: To design and build skillfully
senses.definition: to plan and construct something using technical knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 运用技术知识规划并建造某物
senses.example: They engineered a new water system.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设计建造了一套新的供水系统。
senses.why: The person's skill becomes an action, so the verb names the designing and building itself.
senses.whyCN: 人的技能变成动作，因此动词命名设计与建造本身。

senses.title: To arrange or bring about cleverly
senses.definition: to arrange an event or result through careful planning
senses.definitionCN: 通过周密计划安排事件或结果
senses.example: The team engineered a surprise win.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍巧妙策划了一场意外的胜利。
senses.why: Engineering is careful design, so the verb extends to planning any outcome.
senses.whyCN: 工程就是精心设计，因此动词扩展到策划任何结果。
